sb_prompt: DISCUSS THE CHANGES IN THE ROLES OF WOMEN IN AMERICAN SOCIETY OVER THE PAST GENERATION OR TWO.  WHICH CHANGES HAVE BEEN THE MOST SIGNIFICANT? DO YOU HAVE AN OPINION ON WHAT FURTHER CHANGES WILL TAKE PLACE OVER THE NEXT GENERATION?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Is this... a good time to talk?
ParticipantB: Yeah, sure. Go ahead.
ParticipantA: I got this call to chat about women's roles in America. It's actually kind of a big deal to me.
ParticipantB: Oh, sure. I've heard that before. What's up with that?
ParticipantA: Well, looking back, it's wild. My mom worked in a factory when I was a kid, but she left after one year. She said it was just too hard balancing it all.
ParticipantB: Right. That sounds tough. I never thought about it that way.
ParticipantA: And now? Look at my sister. She's thirty-five and has two masters degrees and a CEO job. She actually manages the whole branch where I work sometimes.
ParticipantB: Whoa. That's a jump from your mom though. Did she ever want to go back to work?
ParticipantA: No, not really. She just wanted to raise us. But my sister? She says she wouldn't trade it. She thinks women should be everywhere.
ParticipantB: Hmm. I guess that makes sense now that I think about it. Though, I've always kind of felt... unsure about it.
ParticipantA: Unsure? Like what?
ParticipantB: I just... I don't know. It feels like a lot of pressure now. Like everyone has to be perfect at everything.
ParticipantA: Maybe it does. But it's also freeing. My sister says she can do what she wants without asking for permission.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I get that. Freedom is good. But sometimes it feels like we're all running in circles trying to prove ourselves.
ParticipantA: That's true. Do you have a girlfriend or anything?
ParticipantB: Yeah, I do. Actually, she's a car mechanic too. Like me.
ParticipantA: Wait, really? Two mechanics in your life?
ParticipantB: Yep. We both love engines. She says women are just as good at fixing cars as men.
ParticipantA: That's interesting. My sister says she's better at customer service than some of the guys. She handles the bank clients all the time.
ParticipantB: Oh, you work at a bank?
ParticipantA: Yeah, I'm a teller. It's quiet, but I see a lot. People treat me differently than they treated my mom.
ParticipantB: How so?
ParticipantA: They assume I can do math and talk to strangers. My mom couldn't do that. She felt like she wasn't allowed to.
ParticipantB: Hmm. That's a shift. Maybe people just expect more of us now.
ParticipantA: Definitely. But do you think we're going too far? Like, is it getting too intense?
ParticipantB: I'm not sure. I just feel like... maybe we need to slow down a bit. Not everyone wants to be a boss or a fixer. Some just want to garden or read.
ParticipantA: Oh, I totally agree on that. My sister does volunteer work now. She says being a leader is exhausting sometimes.
ParticipantB: Exactly. Maybe the next generation will be more balanced. Less "have to," more "want to."
ParticipantA: That sounds nice. No pressure to prove anything.
ParticipantB: Yeah. Just be who you are.
ParticipantA: I like that idea. Well, thanks for talking about this.
ParticipantB: Sure thing. Good chatting.
ParticipantA: You too!
